submitter: deferred_work_item_park lane (bugs_open/396) - the status_override allow-list; the SECOND of two changes, after the park verb (corr ed821065)
rationale:
bugs_open/396, second and smaller half. `status_override` is a step-config key read by FailWorkItemAction (load_work_item_actions.go) as a bare string and written STRAIGHT into site_work_items.status:

    UPDATE site_work_items SET error = $2, status = $3, handled_by = $4 WHERE id = $1

No allow-list, no enum, no CHECK constraint, and no validation against ANY of the three predicates that decide whether a row can ever move again: dispatch claims status IN ('triaged','approved') (claim_work_item_action.go), the promoter selects status='detected', and idx_swi_dedup's exclusion list is (complete, verified, rejected, wont_fix, failed, unresolved, cancelled). A value outside the first two and inside the third's KEPT set leaves the row undispatchable, un-promotable AND still holding its (site_id,item_key) slot - so the detector cannot re-file it and any other session dispatching that page hits 23505, a failure that reads as "already queued" and means "queued and abandoned".

Note the UPDATE leaves handler_agent untouched, so such a row keeps a real handler name, a real priority and a real item_key and carries an error explaining the refusal. It reads as a queued job that hit a snag. There is no tell.

'deferred' is the natural word to reach for when you mean "park this" and is precisely the wrong one - it is the ONE status that is neither claimable, nor promotable, nor terminal. That is the exact shape of the 52 unattributable parked rows bugs_open/396 documents.

THIS IS NOT THE CAUSE OF THOSE 52 AND I AM NOT CLAIMING IT IS. FailWorkItemAction stamps handled_by = agentType and 0 of the 52 carry it; the 52 were made by hand at a psql prompt (their writers' own handoffs and commit messages record it). This key is the door by which the same black hole could be minted AUTOMATICALLY, at production rate, from a single config edit - which is worth closing before it is walked through rather than after.

BLAST RADIUS IS ZERO AND IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. A recursive walk over EVERY agent_definitions row - snapshots and soft-deleted INCLUDED - finds status_override on 4 steps in 3 agents (component-template-fixer x2, page-build-handler, tool-improver) and every single one is 'needs_human_review'. No other value has ever been configured in the estate's history. So this narrows a capability nobody uses.

plan.summary: Add an allow-list for FailWorkItemAction's `status_override` and refuse anything outside it. The rule each entry must meet is stated and tested: a status may be written here only if the row can still LEAVE it - either it is terminal (so it releases the dedup slot and the detector can re-file) or something named moves it on. `deferred` is deliberately excluded and the refusal message points at the park verb (migration 621, WII-034) instead. The fail direction is deliberate: an unrecognised value is REFUSED and the item falls through to the normal failure ladder, which ages and retries it - honouring an unknown status can strand a row for ever, falling back costs at most one attempt. The refusal writes a WORK_ITEM_STATUS_OVERRIDE_REFUSED row to agent_error_log naming the misconfigured step, because a silent narrowing would be its own version of this bug.

edits.rationale: The list goes beside its three existing siblings (terminal / closed / revalidatable), which are already documented as a comparison table so the differences are visible rather than discovered. Adding a fourth row to that table is the cheapest way to stop the next reader inventing a fifth spelling.
edits.sketch: var workItemStatusOverrideAllowed = []string{"needs_human_review","blocked","wont_fix","unresolved","cancelled"} — with the comparison table extended and EACH entry naming its exit: needs_human_review (HandleRetryWorkItem + the resolve endpoint both take it), blocked (the feasibility-recheck scheduled task selects it), and three terminal statuses that release the dedup slot. Plus func statusOverrideAllowed(s string) bool, and const statusOverrideRefusedCode = "WORK_ITEM_STATUS_OVERRIDE_REFUSED" — its own code rather than a generic one because a reader querying it wants the misconfigured STEP, not a failure.

edits.rationale: The guard at the door itself. Refusing and falling through to the ladder is the safe direction; the alternative (returning an error) would fail a live workflow at runtime over a config typo, which is a worse trade than one extra attempt.
edits.sketch: if statusOverride != "" && !statusOverrideAllowed(statusOverride) { logger.Error(...); LogActionEntry(ctx, params, agenterrors.Entry{ErrorCode: statusOverrideRefusedCode, Severity: "error", ErrorMessage: "...is not a status this item could ever leave - refused, and the item was routed through the normal failure ladder instead... To PARK work deliberately use park_work_items() (migration 621, WII-034)", Context: {work_item_id, status_override, allowed, bug}}, logger); statusOverride = "" } — the existing `if statusOverride != ""` branch below is then simply not taken, so the item flows into the ladder that already exists.

edits.rationale: Five tests, written against the mutation that actually matters - which is NOT 'someone deletes the guard' but 'someone adds deferred to the list because it is the natural word for park this'. All five were mutation-proven before submission: each was made to FAIL and then restored.
edits.sketch: TestStatusOverrideRefusesDeferred (mutation: add 'deferred' -> FAILS, verified). TestStatusOverrideEveryEntryHasAnExit - every entry must be terminal or in a namedConsumer map whose values name the live consumer (mutation: add any exitless status -> FAILS, verified). TestStatusOverrideAllowsTheOnlyValueEverConfigured - guards the OPPOSITE direction, an allow-list narrowed until it breaks production (mutation: remove needs_human_review -> FAILS, verified). TestStatusOverrideRejectsUnknown. TestFailWorkItemActionCallsTheGuard - proves the list is WIRED, ⚠ by parsing the AST with parser.ParseFile(..., 0) so comments are DROPPED, because a source-scan test makes your own comments load-bearing and would pass vacuously on the comment that explains the guard (mutation: replace the condition with `if false` leaving every comment in place -> FAILS, verified).

grounded_in: load_work_item_actions.go, the status_override branch: statusOverride, _ := params.StepConfig.Config["status_override"].(string) ... UPDATE site_work_items SET error = $2, status = $3, handled_by = $4 WHERE id = $1 -- a bare config string written straight into status, and handler_agent is not among the columns it writes.

claim_work_item_action.go, read at HEAD: UPDATE site_work_items SET status='claimed' ... WHERE id = $1 AND status IN ('triaged','approved') AND attempt_count < max_attempts -- dispatch filters on STATUS.

idx_swi_dedup from pg_indexes: UNIQUE (site_id, item_key) WHERE item_key IS NOT NULL AND status <> ALL (ARRAY['complete','verified','rejected','wont_fix','failed','unresolved','cancelled']) -- 'deferred' is absent, so a row written to it keeps its slot.

[MEASURED 2026-08-25] recursive walk over EVERY agent_definitions row, snapshots and soft-deleted INCLUDED: status_override appears on 4 steps in 3 agents (component-template-fixer>judged_refusal, component-template-fixer>park_refused, page-build-handler>mark_needs_review, tool-improver>refuse_mangled_write) and EVERY value is 'needs_human_review'. Zero other values in the estate's entire history. Blast radius of the allow-list is therefore zero.

⚠ THE WALK MUST BE RECURSIVE: a flat jsonb_each over default_config->'workflow'->'steps' misses every step nested in a sub_workflow. The same trap cost this lane a wrong reading earlier the same day on a different key (it returned 2 of 5 armed seam steps and read as 'the migration half-reverted').

bugs_open/396 worked cost of the shape this key can mint: a page_rerender parked at 'deferred' with attempt_count=0 sat 22 days, blocked bugs_open/328's dispatch with 23505, and completed 2 minutes after being re-armed to 'triaged'.

This key is NOT the cause of the 52 unattributable rows and the submission does not claim it: FailWorkItemAction stamps handled_by = agentType and 0 of the 52 carry it (CONTROL: handled_by is populated on 7,114 of 7,329 'complete' rows, so that zero is a real absence and not a dead column). The 52 were hand-parked; their writers' own handoffs and commit message 90a4fb812 record it.

work_items_common.go already documents three sibling status lists as a comparison table, with an explicit warning that only workItemTerminalStatuses may be interpolated into an ON CONFLICT clause because only it matches idx_swi_dedup's predicate - migration 157 broke that pair once fleet-wide with SQLSTATE 42P10. The new list is NOT interpolated into any index-bearing clause; it is a plain Go membership test.

The estate's existing test for FailWorkItemAction (work_item_failure_ladder_test.go) is a SOURCE SCAN over the file text. LANDMINES records that a source-scanning test makes your comments load-bearing and can pass vacuously on the needle matching your own comment - which is why TestFailWorkItemActionCallsTheGuard parses the AST with comments dropped instead, and why the mutation used to prove it (`if false`, comments untouched) is the one that would defeat a grep.

Owner ruling 2026-08-02 (RFC_010 section 2): a comment is not a control on a tree this many sessions share. The four live status_override values agree by CONVENTION, not by CONSTRAINT - this change makes the agreement mechanical.

migration 621 / register WII-034 (park_work_items), shipped by this same lane today: the refusal message points callers there, so the narrowing removes a bad way to park and names the good one in the same breath rather than just saying no.
